ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that lines $AB$ and $CD$ intersect at point $O$, and $\angle COE = 90^\circ$. If $\angle AOC = 37^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle BOE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\because \angle COE=90^\circ$, $\angle AOC=37^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle BOE=180^\circ-\angle AOC-\angle COE$ \\
$=180^\circ-37^\circ-90^\circ$ \\
$=\boxed{53^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, point O is the intersection point of three rays/straight lines; the horizontal straight line passes through C, O, D, with C on the left side of O and D on the right side of O; the oblique straight line passes through A, O, B, with A at the lower left of O and B at the upper right of O, so A, O, B are collinear; from O upward there is ray OE, with E above O. In the figure, a right-angle mark is drawn between OC and OE, corresponding to ∠COE = 90°. Reasoning: according to a straight-angle path in the figure from ray OA to ray OB, it passes through the adjacent angles ∠AOC, ∠COE, ∠EOB in sequence. Because A, O, B are collinear, ∠AOB = 180°. It is given that ∠AOC = 37°, ∠COE = 90°, therefore ∠BOE = ∠EOB = 180° - 37° - 90° = 53°.
